from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide", 
                          ["Classical bits are either zero or one.", 
                           "Quantum states exist in a continuum.", 
                           "Think of a dimmer light switch."])
        
        # Objects
        bit_0 = Text("0", color=BLUE).scale(1.5)
        bit_1 = Text("1", color=RED).scale(1.5)
        quantum_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#FFFF00")
        quantum_label = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle", color="#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(bit_0, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(bit_1, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(bit_0), FadeIn(bit_1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(FadeOut(bit_0), FadeOut(bit_1))
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE).set_stroke(opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_vec, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_label, 'B3')
        self.play(GrowArrow(quantum_vec), Write(quantum_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        dimmer = Slider(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, length=3, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dimmer, 'E3')
        self.play(Create(dimmer))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

class Slider(VGroup):
    def __init__(self, start, end, length, **kwargs):
        super().__init__()
        line = Line(start=start, end=end, **kwargs)
        line.set_length(length)
        knob = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.add(line, knob)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Bloch Sphere visualizes quantum states.",
            "The vector points to any surface coordinate.",
            "Rotation around the sphere represents phase."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: The Bloch Sphere", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create Bloch Sphere objects
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.5, fill_opacity=0.1, color=WHITE).set_stroke(width=1)
        axes = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        label_psi = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle", color=YELLOW).next_to(vector.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Combine into a group to place on grid
        bloch_group = VGroup(sphere, axes, vector, label_psi)
        self.place_at_grid(bloch_group, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(sphere), Create(axes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector), Write(label_psi))
        self.play(Rotate(vector, angle=PI/2, axis=RIGHT, about_point=ORIGIN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Rotate(vector, angle=2*PI, axis=UP, about_point=ORIGIN))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Measurement forces a collapse to basis states.",
            "The Born rule calculates the probability.",
            "Opening the box determines the outcome."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Collapse: Measurement and Reality", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        state_vec = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        state_label = MathTex(r"|\psi\rangle = \alpha|0\rangle + \beta|1\rangle").next_to(state_vec, UP)
        basis_0 = MathTex(r"|0\rangle").move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        basis_1 = MathTex(r"|1\rangle").move_to(self.grid["E3"])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display state vector |ψ⟩ before measurement.
        self.play(Create(state_vec), Write(state_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate measurement operation on state vector.
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_0), FadeIn(basis_1))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show vector collapse to |0⟩ or |1⟩ in #FF0000.
        collapse_anim = state_vec.animate.set_color(RED).move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(collapse_anim)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Quantum Computing", [
            "Superposition enables parallel computation.",
            "Qubits explore multiple paths simultaneously.",
            "This drastically speeds up complex calculations."
        ])
        
        # --- Mobjects ---
        # Circuit for Lecture 1
        circuit = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*1, RIGHT*1),
            Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT*0.2),
            Dot(LEFT*1), Dot(RIGHT*1)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(circuit, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Qubit/Paths for Lecture 2
        qubit = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        paths = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, UP*1+RIGHT*i) for i in [-0.5, 0, 0.5]])
        
        # Graph for Lecture 3
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], x_length=3, y_length=2).add_coordinates()
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(-(x-2)**2), color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(circuit))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(paths), FadeIn(qubit))
        self.play(qubit.animate.move_to(paths[1].get_end()))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(graph, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Superposition and Quantum States: The Architecture of Quantum Reality

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
sections.content: Define the classical state (binary: 0 or 1) versus the quantum state (a continuum). Introduce the vector representation on a complex plane (Bloch Sphere) to visualize how quantum states exist beyond simple switches.
sections.example: A classical light switch is ON or OFF. A quantum light switch is a dimmer slider that can be set to any position between ON and OFF simultaneously.

sections.title: Defining Superposition: The Mathematical Foundation
sections.content: Introduce the Dirac notation |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Explain that α and β are complex probability amplitudes where |α|² + |β|² = 1. Focus on the idea that superposition is a linear combination, not a mixture of two separate states.
sections.example: Think of a spinning coin. While it's spinning, it is not 'Heads' or 'Tails', but a mathematical blend of both until it hits the table.

sections.title: Visualization: The Bloch Sphere
sections.content: Use a 3D animated sphere graphic. Show the state vector pointing to different coordinates to represent the superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩. Explain how rotation represents phase changes.
sections.example: Imagine an arrow starting at the North Pole (State |0⟩) and rotating to the equator (a perfect 50/50 superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩).

sections.title: The Collapse: Measurement and Reality
sections.content: Explain that measurement 'forces' a system into a basis state. Discuss the Born rule—the probability of finding the particle in state |0⟩ is |α|². This is the bridge between the quantum 'cloud' and classical experience.
sections.example: Schrödinger’s Cat: The box contains a cat in a superposition of |Alive⟩ and |Dead⟩. Opening the box (measurement) collapses the state vector into one of the two classical realities.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Quantum Computing
sections.content: Briefly connect superposition to parallel computation. By existing in a superposition, a qubit explores multiple computational paths simultaneously, drastically reducing the time required for specific complex calculations.
sections.example: A maze-solving robot: A classical robot tests paths one by one; a quantum robot in superposition walks all paths at once to find the exit instantly.
